title: Exact values of the record sides for n = 88, 126, 172, 199, 263 (minimal polynomials): registration request
body:
**Credit name.** Hyukdong Kim (ORCID [0000-0001-5787-8066](https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5787-8066)), with Claude (Anthropic) as computational assistant (see *AI assistance*).

**Claim.** The side of the current record packing at each count below is the real algebraic number given, as a root of the stated polynomial, which is irreducible over Q. At each count, the register (jlevy/squares at `2ec489d1eede791bf0686ca1c524278c2bb80253`) records `minimal_polynomial: null`. The atlas exact-form table (evand/square-packing at `659ee62e4a9d39542a1146e8b011cc3ab6407ede`, `search/exact/EXACT_FORMS.md`) lists each count as `open`.

| n | record side (register) | degree | exact value | root used |
|---:|---|---:|---|---|
| 88 | 9.8824510304812469 | 7 | root of P₈₈ | 4th of 5 real roots |
| 126 | 11.7426406871192852 | 2 | **15/2 + 3√2** (4s² − 60s + 153 = 0) | larger root |
| 172 | 13.6189889568993984289 | 24 | root of P₁₇₂ | 1st of 4 real roots |
| 199 | 14.6175721735928069 | 16 | root of P₁₉₉ | 2nd of 2 real roots |
| 263 | 16.73316600789937898 | 17 | root of P₂₆₃ | only real root |

Why these were open: in all five records the tilted band is not pinned by its contacts alone. The contact equations leave free directions, and the side is fixed by stationarity of the minimization, as for s(5) and s(51). The atlas table reports these cases as "more unknowns than consistency polynomials", a timeout, or a memory cap. Adding the KKT stationarity equations to the contact equations closes the system, and the resulting degrees (2 to 24) are low.

For n = 126, the exact side 15/2 + 3√2 = 11.742640687119285146405… lies about 1.2·10⁻²² below the current verified rational upper bound 11742640687119285146522492579501/10³⁰. An exact certificate of the packing at this side would tighten the verified bound accordingly; I have not produced one (see *Not done*).

**Certificate.** This is a numerical determination, not an exact certificate. The bundle contains `exact_forms.json` (polynomials and 100-digit values), `verify_exact_forms.py` with its four modules (`lppolish.py`, `exactform.py`, `kkt.py`, `kkt_fast.py`) and a README. It is attached to this issue as `squares-exact-forms.zip`, SHA-256 `c770f9c37dee6b248543f3e661318630a0f279bc6a8c7663cb2efc53e2814ee7`. The attachment is fixed once posted; the hash pins its content.
([squares-exact-forms.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33917140/squares-exact-forms.zip))


Method, per count:

1. Read the record packing from evand/square-packing `site/www/data/p/best-<n>.json` at the pinned revision.
2. Polish to a local optimum. With the angles fixed, every chosen separating-axis constraint and every wall constraint is linear, so minimizing the side is an exact LP; the angles move by trust-region SLP. The side changes by less than 1e-14.
3. Collect every active contact at tolerance 1e-9: square–square contacts on their separating axis, and square–wall contacts. The |cos| and |sin| kinks are resolved into sign branches, and both branches are kept when the argument sits on a kink, which encodes parallel or upright squares.
4. Solve the KKT system g(z) = 0, e_s = Σ λ_k ∇g_k(z) for all coordinates, angles, the side and the multipliers. The solver is minimum-norm Newton with a frozen double-precision pseudo-inverse and residuals evaluated in arb.
5. Find the polynomial at 1500 digits by LLL on (1, s, …, s^d), using FLINT's fmpz_mat.lll, and reduce it to its irreducible factor vanishing at s.
6. Re-solve the KKT system independently from the start at 3000 digits.

**Checking.**
- At 3000 digits, with the side re-solved from scratch, |P(s)| is about 10⁻³⁰⁰⁰ for all five: 10⁻³⁰⁰¹ (88), 10⁻³⁰⁰⁷ (126), 10⁻²⁹⁸⁸ (172), 10⁻³⁰⁰³ (199), 10⁻²⁹⁹³ (263). The KKT residuals are 10⁻³⁰⁰¹ to 10⁻³⁰¹¹. A spurious LLL relation found at 1500 digits would fail here at about 10⁻¹⁵⁰⁰.
- Re-solving from a start perturbed by 1e-9 gives the same side to all working digits, so the side is pinned by the KKT system.
- Irreducibility over Q (sympy) holds for all five. Exact real-root isolation (sympy) gives the roots above, which agree with the solved side to at least 55 digits.
- `python verify_exact_forms.py <atlas>/site/www/data/p 400` reruns steps 1–4 from the raw atlas coordinates and checks the claimed polynomials. It prints `ALL OK` and takes about 2.5 minutes on 2 CPU cores. At 3000 digits it takes about 25 minutes.
- The multipliers are not unique (redundant contacts). In the minimum-norm solution the smallest is about −6·10⁻¹⁶, i.e. zero to double precision; a nonnegative multiplier vector was found by NNLS at double precision, but nonnegativity was not certified.

**What the checkers share.** Everything here is one code base by one author. The discovery run (1500 digits) and the confirmation run (3000 digits) share the active-set extraction from double-precision coordinates and the KKT formulation, so a wrong active set would affect both. They differ only in precision and in being solved independently. Irreducibility and root isolation use sympy, which is independent of the solver.

**Not done.**
- No exact or interval certificate. The arb values are used as multiprecision midpoints, and the ball radii are not carried as rigorous enclosures.
- No proof that the extracted active set and sign branches are the right ones, beyond the numerical agreement with the record side (within 3·10⁻¹⁵ at every count) and the convergence of the KKT system.
- These are exact values of the record sides, i.e. upper bounds only, not optimality claims. No Lean formalization.

Related negative results, LLL at 1500 digits on the KKT-solved side: for n = 55, 130 and 179, no relation of degree ≤ 80; for n = 110, 131, 132, 155, 156, 180, 181, 182, 208–211, 228 and 235–241, no relation of degree ≤ 70. In each case LLL returned only a generic-size vector (about 10¹⁹–10²² at the top degree), so no relation with markedly smaller coefficients exists. For n = 105 the KKT iteration did not converge from the extracted active set. For n = 154, 270 and 303 the atlas coordinates lag the register, so those were not run.

**Lineage and credit.** The packings are the current records, credited as in `claimed_by` of `packing/frontier/n-<n>.md`:
- n = 88 and n = 199: Nate Chaoweeraprasit (itsnaka) and Siddharth Gupta.
- n = 126: Ryan Xu and Evan Daniel.
- n = 172: Francisco Couzo, Evan Daniel and PingYou Ltd.
- n = 263: PingYou Ltd, Nate Chaoweeraprasit (itsnaka) and Evan Daniel.

This result only identifies the exact value of their sides. The open status comes from Evan Daniel's exact-form pipeline in evand/square-packing. The method — KKT closure for stationary records, then LLL — is new in this submission as far as I know.

**AI assistance.** The search for open cases, the KKT/LLL pipeline, the computations and the verification script were done by Claude (Anthropic, model Claude Opus 5.5) in a chat session at my direction. I reviewed the outputs and am submitting them.
